title: Direct ionization limits sharp X-ray ingress in a freely shearing ASASSN-14ko screen
abstract: We test the physical cost of a sharp repeated X-ray ingress in one circular screen model for ASASSN-14ko. Positive radial extinction depths add before flux is calculated. We combine this serial transfer with a direct-ionization density limit and derive a bound on the rate at which electron column can enter each ray. The bound allows any radial density profile below the ionization envelope. For a one-percent annulus at the 108.44-day circular radius, a reference mass of 10^7.86 solar masses and xi at least 10^4 erg cm/s, a cycle-14 fall from 80 to 5 percent direct flux within two days needs ionizing luminosity of at least 1.03e47 erg/s. Exact Gaussian-source calculations at 1e47 and 3e47 erg/s give transition widths of 2.559 and 1.645 days. Thus arbitrary optical depth is not a free escape from shear when direct ionization limits density. This is a conditional model bound, not an observed luminosity or a measured screen age. Cold absorption, screen reset, trapped radiation, noncircular motion, confined gas and scattered-light changes remain outside the test. Code, proof, synthetic results, source hashes and checks are supplied.

display.caption: Necessary ionizing luminosity and exact synthetic direct-beam ingress curves for the specified shearing annulus. The transition thresholds are model test requirements, not new measurements.
